name: v39_backlog_inventory_conversion_vecavg
hypothesis: Order backlog growth is only useful if it converts through inventory turnover and lower receivable intensity; corrected vector handling tests whether v38 failed because of expression type rather than weak economics.
expression: 0.45 * group_rank(ts_rank(ts_delta(vec_avg(fnd6_obs), 252) / assets, 126), industry) + 0.25 * group_rank(ts_rank(inventory_turnover, 126), subindustry) + 0.20 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * receivable / sales, 126), subindustry) + 0.10 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * (correlation_last_60_days_spy - correlation_last_360_days_spy), 60), industry)
notes: Corrected v38 order backlog via vec_avg; removes partner breadth from weak v26 backlog expression.

name: v39_backlog_margin_cash_conversion
hypothesis: Rising backlog should be more valuable when gross margin and operating cash conversion are also healthy.
expression: 0.40 * group_rank(ts_rank(ts_delta(vec_avg(fnd6_obs), 252) / assets, 126), industry) + 0.25 * group_rank(ts_rank(fnd6_newa1v1300_gp / sales, 126), subindustry) + 0.20 * group_rank(ts_rank(cashflow_op / assets, 126), industry) + 0.15 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * (systematic_risk_last_60_days - systematic_risk_last_360_days), 60), industry)
notes: Backlog with cash/margin conversion; watch correlation with RRp7Q9Le and cashflow/accounting ACTIVE set.

name: v39_inventory_mix_vector_raw_vs_finished
hypothesis: Raw-material inventory above finished-goods inventory can be constructive demand preparation, while finished-goods accumulation is more likely unsold product.
expression: 0.40 * group_rank(ts_rank((vec_avg(fnd6_newqeventv110_invrmq) - vec_avg(fnd6_newqeventv110_invfgq)) / assets, 126), industry) + 0.25 * group_rank(ts_rank(inventory_turnover, 126), subindustry) + 0.20 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * receivable / sales, 126), subindustry) + 0.15 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * (beta_last_60_days_spy - beta_last_360_days_spy), 60), industry)
notes: Corrected v38 inventory event vectors with vec_avg before subtract.

name: v39_inventory_mix_matrix_raw_vs_finished
hypothesis: The matrix inventory taxonomy may be cleaner than event-vector inventory; raw-material intensity minus finished-goods intensity should prefer firms preparing for future production over firms carrying unsold goods.
expression: 0.45 * group_rank(ts_rank((fnd6_newqv1300_invrmq - fnd6_newqv1300_invfgq) / assets, 126), industry) + 0.25 * group_rank(ts_rank(inventory_turnover, 126), subindustry) + 0.15 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * receivable / sales, 126), subindustry) + 0.15 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * (systematic_risk_last_60_days - systematic_risk_last_360_days), 60), industry)
notes: Matrix alternative to vector inventory; should avoid event-input operator errors.

name: v39_finished_goods_overhang_matrix
hypothesis: Lower finished-goods inventory relative to sales, combined with stable turnover and low receivables, may capture clean sell-through.
expression: 0.45 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * fnd6_newqv1300_invfgq / sales, 126), industry) + 0.25 * group_rank(ts_rank(inventory_turnover, 126), subindustry) + 0.20 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * receivable / sales, 126), subindustry) + 0.10 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * (correlation_last_60_days_spy - correlation_last_360_days_spy), 60), industry)
notes: Simple finished-goods overhang probe; likely correlates with LLp7PRmM if too receivable-heavy.

name: v39_restructuring_low_noise_backlog_vecavg
hypothesis: Low restructuring charges with positive backlog should favor clean demand over turnaround situations.
expression: 0.45 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * vec_avg(fnd6_newqeventv110_rcpq) / assets, 126), industry) + 0.30 * group_rank(ts_rank(vec_avg(fnd6_obs) / assets, 126), industry) + 0.15 * group_rank(ts_rank(inventory_turnover, 126), subindustry) + 0.10 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * (unsystematic_risk_last_60_days - unsystematic_risk_last_360_days), 60), industry)
notes: Corrected v38 restructuring/backlog vector inputs with vec_avg.

name: v39_restructuring_reversal_clean_matrix
hypothesis: Low restructuring cost with less working-capital bloat can identify firms without special-charge noise and balance-sheet stress.
expression: 0.45 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * fnd6_newqv1300_rcpq / assets, 126), industry) + 0.25 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * working_capital / assets, 126), industry) + 0.20 * group_rank(ts_rank(inventory_turnover, 126), subindustry) + 0.10 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * (correlation_last_60_days_spy - correlation_last_360_days_spy), 60), industry)
notes: Matrix version of low restructuring noise; no order backlog to separate whether backlog itself adds value.

name: v39_clean_operating_cycle_matrix
hypothesis: Higher payable support, lower receivables, and lower finished-goods overhang should capture a clean operating cycle without relying on earnings, sales estimates, graph, close/open, or option fields.
expression: 0.35 * group_rank(ts_rank(fnd6_cptnewqv1300_apq / assets, 126), industry) + 0.25 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * fnd6_newqv1300_rectrq / sales, 126), subindustry) + 0.25 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * fnd6_newqv1300_invfgq / sales, 126), subindustry) + 0.15 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * (beta_last_60_days_spy - beta_last_360_days_spy), 60), industry)
notes: Pure matrix working-capital cycle probe; compare to v38 supplier financing and LLp7PRmM receivables ACTIVE.
